hero.caption: View of the Kīlauea summit eruption in Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park, from the south rim of the caldera. The caldera wall behind the erupting vents is approximately 210 meters (690 feet) tall.  This morning, USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory field crews reported lava fountain heights of 50 meters (160 feet) and 40 m (140 feet) from north and south vents, respectively. At about 8:25 a.m. this morning, field crews reported that parts of the south vent collapsed, with an associated reduction of about half in south vent lava fountain height. Lava flow activity has remained confined to the southwest crater floor area near the active vents.

images.filename: Close Up Image of a Topographical Map of Eastern Hawaiʻi (2698530a-64e8-45e2-8e85-ad7e46a78689).tif
images.caption:
A black and white close-up image of Charles Wilkes' topographical map of Hawaiʻi island showing Kīlauea's and Mauna Loa's craters. Towards the bottom right corner of the image, there is a section of lower Puna's coastline. Towns are labeled next to black dots which indicate their location. It also has roughly drawn lines indicating roads/trails around Kīlauea and Mauna Loa. There are circles and outlines of the various craters of Kīlauea and Mauna Loa. They are labeled. Around Mauna Loa crater there are a series of elevation lines going out from the crater to indicate elevation changes in the landscape.
A close-up image of Charles Wilkes' topographical map of Hawaiʻi island showing Kīlauea's and Mauna Loa's craters.

images.filename: A Copy of Lieutenant Charles George Malden's Map of Kīlauea Cra (caafcd66-61dc-4c34-ab83-6d7f5ed4c713).tif
images.caption:
A black and white image of an 1825 map of Kīlauea crater created by British lieutenant Charles Robert Malden. In the top left corner of the map is a reference list. In the top center of the image is the title of the map. It reads, " A p. e. a. n. of the Volcano Peli in the island of Owhyhee by Lieu. Malden, R. C. 1825." Below the title is a "Scale of Three English Miles." The map itself is shaped like an oval leaning towards the right side of the image. Near the top of the oval there is an extension going towards the right of the image to another smaller oval shape. There is a bumpy border around the edge of the crater. On the floor of the crater there are black dots, circles, and thick lines. These are labeled by numbers 1-6 corresponding to the references list. On the top side of the large crater closest to "references" is the number "7" located near a cliff edge. There are highlights and labels of various shadings and drawings on and around the map. Below the map there is a thin cross shape compass.
A copy of a 1825 map of Kīlauea crater created by British lieutenant Charles Robert Malden.
